$comment: VANISH BROKER REGISTRY — static, version-controlled reference data (PRD §16).
This is NOT user data. Adding coverage = adding a record, no code change.
ORDERING MATTERS. The list is ordered by value to the user, not alphabetically:
sites where you can actually SEE your own record for free come first, because
that is where someone gets the 'oh, there I am' moment that makes the rest of
the work worth doing. Paywalled sites still matter — your data is still there —
but they come later.
PROVENANCE — every record carries `source`:
'ca-registry' — the opt-out route is taken from the broker's own annual filing
with the California Privacy Protection Agency under the Delete Act (SB 362).
https://cppa.ca.gov/data_broker_registry/complete-reg-data-brokers.csv
A legal declaration, published as machine-readable CSV. Authoritative.
'published' — the broker's publicly documented opt-out page. Used for sites
that are NOT in California's registry but are too important to a user to
leave out (several of the biggest free people-search sites are in this
group). Confirm on arrival; every one of these carries a footer fallback
in its note.
THE VERIFICATION RULE, refined:
optOutMethod 'email' REQUIRES source 'ca-registry'. A wrong email address
fails SILENTLY — the request goes nowhere and the user believes they are done.
That is the failure mode this project exists to prevent, so it gets the
strict bar.
optOutMethod 'link' may use source 'published'. A wrong URL fails VISIBLY —
the user sees a 404 and can fall back to the footer link, which the note tells
them to do. Visible failure is recoverable; silent failure is not.
scanStrategy — see docs/SCAN-VIABILITY.md for the measurements behind this:
'html-parse' — the broker serves search results to a plain request AND gives a
different response for a real name than for an impossible one. Exactly one
broker passes that test: Spokeo.
'assisted'   — everything else. The user opens the search link in their own
browser and pastes back the listing URL. Vanish does NOT attempt to defeat
bot detection (out of scope, PRD §4.2).
freeToView — can the user see that they are listed without paying or
registering? Drives the 'free to view' badge. Honest expectation-setting: a
paywalled site still holds your data and the opt-out still works, but you may
not get to read the record first.

brokers.name: TruePeopleSearch
brokers.note: One of the most exposing sites on this list — full address history, phone numbers and relatives, free and with no signup. Start here. If the removal link has moved, look for "Remove My Record" in their footer. Not registered with California, so treat the link as published-not-filed.

brokers.name: FastPeopleSearch
brokers.note: Same shape as TruePeopleSearch and frequently carries the same records — free, detailed, no signup. If the removal link has moved, look for "Remove My Record" in their footer.

brokers.name: ThatsThem
brokers.note: Free and unusually detailed — often shows email addresses and IP-derived location alongside the usual address and phone. If the opt-out link has moved, look for "Opt Out" in their footer.

brokers.name: Cyber Background Checks
brokers.note: Free to view, including relatives and past addresses. If the removal link has moved, look for "Remove My Info" in their footer.

brokers.name: Advanced Background Checks
brokers.note: Free to view. If the removal link has moved, look for "Remove My Record" in their footer.

brokers.name: USPhonebook
brokers.note: Phone-number focused and free to view. Worth doing if your number has ever been public. If the opt-out link has moved, look for "Opt Out" in their footer.

brokers.name: ClustrMaps
brokers.note: Indexes people against street addresses, so it tends to expose where you have lived rather than who you are. Free to view. If the opt-out link has moved, look for "Opt Out" in their footer.

brokers.name: Radaris
brokers.note: Large and mostly free to view. Radaris has historically asked you to claim the profile before removing it — if it demands an account, stop and use the phone or email route on their contact page instead. Not registered with California.

brokers.name: Nuwber
brokers.note: Free to view. Email is the only opt-out route Nuwber filed with California — there is no form. Send the message below and keep the sent copy.

brokers.name: Spokeo
brokers.note: The one site Vanish can check for you automatically. Shows that a record exists free, but paywalls the detail. Paste the exact profile URL and your email, then click the link Spokeo emails you — the removal does not take effect until you do. Each listing must be opted out separately.

brokers.name: Whitepages
brokers.note: One of the oldest and most widely indexed. Shows names and partial addresses free. Whitepages has historically asked for phone verification to complete a suppression — if they ask, that's them, not a phishing step.

brokers.name: BeenVerified
brokers.note: High value for one action: this single opt-out also covers PeopleLooker, NeighborWho and NumberGuru, which are the same company. Their privacy policy §19.6 expressly accepts authorized-agent requests.

brokers.name: Intelius
brokers.note: Also covers US Search. Their site route means finding your profile and using the "Do Not Sell My Personal Information" link at the bottom of the page; the email below is the route they filed with California, so it works without hunting for the link.

brokers.name: PeopleFinders
brokers.note: PeopleFinders didn't file a direct opt-out URL — you reach it from the "Do Not Sell My Info" link in their site footer, or from Section V of the privacy policy linked here.

brokers.name: MyLife
brokers.note: Worth doing even though it's unpleasant: MyLife publishes a "reputation score" alongside your record, which is exactly the sort of thing people find when they search your name. If the opt-out link has moved, look for "Do Not Sell My Info" in their footer.

brokers.name: PeekYou
brokers.note: Aggregates social and web profiles against your name rather than address records — a different exposure from the rest of this list, and the one most likely to surface in a casual search of you.

brokers.name: SpyDialer
brokers.note: Reverse phone and name lookup, free. Search from their homepage — they don't use a linkable results URL.

brokers.name: Searchbug
brokers.note: Shows that records exist but charges to open them. The opt-out page is their filed CCPA route.

brokers.name: TruthFinder
brokers.note: Heavily paywalled — you likely won't see your own record without subscribing, but it is there and the opt-out works without paying. Reachable from their homepage as "Do Not Sell My Personal Information".

brokers.name: Instant Checkmate
brokers.note: Same operator as TruthFinder — opting out of one does not opt you out of the other. Do both. Also paywalled for viewing.

brokers.name: PeopleSearcher
brokers.note: Also reachable from their homepage as "Do Not Sell My Info".

brokers.name: Social Catfish
brokers.note: Searches images and social profiles as well as records. Search from their page — they don't use a linkable results URL.

brokers.name: Glad I Know
brokers.note: Smaller than the rest of this list but registered and reachable. Email is the route they filed with California.
